events.what: Chase, Hunter and Tao prove the Gilbreath analogue holds almost surely for a Cramér random model, and give a deterministic inverse theorem describing the only ways a Gilbreath array can fail
Granville preprint claiming 'a precise path to the solution' via reverse sieving, resting on an unproved conjecture about as hard as Gilbreath's
events.credibility_reason: Proof route depends on its Conjecture 5.1(4), of comparable difficulty to the problem itself

events.what: Computational verification up to 10^14 (Plouffe, Oct 2025) and later extensions by Colonna to 1.5×10^15

judgement.doubts: The Chase–Hunter–Tao inverse theorem is genuine unconditional mathematics, but it is a reduction of the conjecture to unproven statements about prime gaps (no long zero-blocks or shallow {0,d}-blocks), not a bound on any quantity the bullet asks about nor a settled case; the random-model result is about a different object. Both are scope variant/none, so nothing moves the status. Gemini only generated figure code: ai_role none.

corrections.why: F3/F4: the record itself says the paper 'does not settle any case of the conjecture for actual primes'; the Cramér-model theorem is a changed question (variant) and the inverse theorem is a reduction to unproven conditions on prime gaps (none), not a bound on a quantity. The verifications are instances and Granville's preprint reduces to an equally hard conjecture. No event survives step 1, so the status is open.
